newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi sticks to sell-off timetable.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi sticks to sell-off timetable.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Friday he was committed to plans to sell off all the state's holding in motorway operator Autostrade before the summer.
In an interview with Il Mondo magazine, released ahead of publication, Ciampi was also quoted as confirming that the third tranche of energy giant ENI will be placed on the market by the summer.
Earlier this week one of the banks helping privatise Autostrade warned that conditions laid down by parliament for the sale risked delaying the operation.
State holding IRI owns some 87 percent of Autostrade. The Treasury holds 69 percent of Eni and is not expected to drop through the 50 percent barrier with the third tranche offering.
"By the summer Autostrade will be completely privatised and the third Eni tranched put on the market," Ciampi was quoted as saying, giving no further details.
Ciampi added that the government remained committed to "the pledge to privatise Stet by the end of 1997".
The sale of state telecoms Stet has been repeatedly delayed by parliament's inability to approve legislation creating a watchdog body for the sector.
The government hopes to get the watchdog bill ratified by the end of the month, but the package is still faced by a barrage of opposition amendments.
Parliament has already passed a bill creating a regulatory authority for electricity utility Enel, but Ciampi declined to fix a date for its sell-off.
"We'll talk about this later on. Technically speaking, we need more time," he said.
By contrast, Ciampi said the Treasury had decided to press ahead with the privatisation of Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, but he gave no precise time.
BNL recently linked up with insurer INA to take a 60 percent stake in loss making Banco di Napoli. The acquisition is due to be completed before the end of the summer.
